subject: literature
passage: In the final round of the regional championship, Adaeze Okafor sat motionless for twenty minutes while her clock ran down, studying a position that looked hopeless to everyone watching. At last she pushed a pawn forward, a move so quiet that her opponent barely glanced at it. Only later, replaying the game with her coach, did she see how narrow her escape had been: if she ______ her bishop instead, as she had nearly done, her opponent could have trapped her king in three moves.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The sentence imagines a past event that did not happen (she did not move the bishop), and the result clause uses "could have trapped." In Standard English, the "if" clause of an unreal past condition uses the past perfect: "if she had moved." "Would have" belongs only in the result clause, never in the "if" clause.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Would have moved" cannot appear in the "if" clause of a conditional; it belongs in the result clause.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The present tense "moves" doesn't fit a past situation that never happened.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The present perfect "has moved" doesn't fit a past situation that never happened.
explanation.D: Correct. The past perfect "had moved" is the standard form for the "if" clause of an unreal past condition.
